binary-search.title: Binary search

steps.n: We start with two pointers: low at the first index and high at the last index.
mid is the average of low and high, so index 3. The value there is 17.
17 is less than the target 21, so everything left of mid can be ignored. low moves to mid + 1.
Now mid is index 5 and the value is 29, which is bigger than 21.
So the target must be on the left. high moves to mid - 1.
mid is now index 4 and arr[4] is exactly 21. The search ends.
The function returned index 4, so print shows 4.

bubble-sort.title: Bubble sort

steps.n: Bubble sort compares two neighbours at a time. First pair is 5 and 2.
5 is bigger than 2, so the two values swap places.
Now compare 5 and 9. They are already in order, so nothing changes.
9 is bigger than 1, so this pair is out of order.
After the swap, 9 has bubbled to the end. It is now in its final place.
The next passes fix 5, then 2 and 1, until the whole list is sorted.
The sorted list is printed.

recursion.title: Recursion: factorial

steps.n: We call factorial with n equal to 3.
n is 3, not 0, so the function calls itself with n - 1.
Now n is 2. It again waits for factorial(1).
When n is 0 the function stops calling itself and returns 1.
The calls return one by one. factorial(1) is 1 times 1, which is 1.
factorial(2) is 2, and factorial(3) is 3 times 2, which is 6.
The final answer 6 is printed.
